transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I just don’t care about my painting or the garden anymore, and the things I used to look forward to feel like a burden. My daughter and my regular doctor really pressed for me to come here because I’ve completely withdrawn from my usual activities and groups.
How long have you been feeling this way, and was there a specific event or time when you noticed your interest in activities and social interactions started to decrease?

This low, uninterested feeling has been going on for about three months now, starting right after I crashed from a very busy, high-energy period in the spring. My husband’s declining health over the past year has been a major stressor, but this complete withdrawal really set in after that hectic spring episode ended.
Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement or return to your normal self since this withdrawal started three months ago, or has it been a consistent low mood and lack of interest?

No, it has been completely constant with no breaks or improvements at all. Ever since I crashed three months ago, this heavy, worn-out feeling has been hanging over me every single day. I just haven't felt like my normal self at all.
Have you experienced any significant weight changes, appetite changes, or sleep disturbances since you started feeling this way three months ago?

Yes, I've really lost my appetite lately, and food just feels like a chore that I have to remind myself to do. My daughter has even pointed out that my clothes are hanging much looser on me than they did a couple of months ago.
Do you often find yourself feeling guilty or worthless about not being able to participate in or enjoy the things you used to, or is that not something that's been bothering you?

I haven't really thought about feeling guilty or worthless, to be honest. I'm mostly just feeling completely empty, tired, and unable to care about my usual activities rather than feeling those specific emotions.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling 'empty' and 'unable to care' - is it that you don't experience any pleasure from activities you used to enjoy, or is it more that you just don't have the energy to participate in them?

It’s really a combination of both, to be honest. I walk past my easel and garden beds and feel absolutely nothing at all—no excitement or urge to pick up a brush. At the same time, I feel completely bone-tired, and even simple daily tasks feel like an immense burden.
Have you experienced episodes like this before in your life, or is this the first time you've felt this persistent low mood and lack of interest in activities?

I don't recall ever feeling quite like this before in my life. This whole pattern of shifting from being so highly revved up in the spring to feeling this low over the last few months is entirely new to me.

You mentioned this is the first time you've felt this way, but can you tell me if you've had any previous episodes of feeling extremely high-energy and productive, like in the spring, followed by a crash, even if the crash wasn't as severe as what you're experiencing now?
No, I don't recall ever having episodes like this before this year. My mood and energy levels have generally been quite stable my whole life until everything changed this past spring.

You've mentioned this is your first experience with such a prolonged low mood, but considering your age and the fact that this episode started after a period of high energy, do you think this could be a single episode or might this be part of a recurring pattern that could emerge over time?

I really don't know if this is going to become a recurring pattern or not. Since this is the first time in my entire life I've ever experienced either that intense high or this deep low, I'm just incredibly confused and overwhelmed by it all. I am hoping with all my heart that it's just a one-time thing, but I really have no idea what to expect.

Given that you've experienced a significant shift from high energy to a low mood this year, and considering this is your first such experience, do you think there might be any factors or stressors in your life that could trigger similar episodes in the future, or does this feel like an isolated incident to you?

The intense stress of caring for my husband's worsening heart and mobility issues, along with the lack of sleep from managing his medications, has been a major trigger. Since those caregiving demands are ongoing and highly stressful, I do worry that this might not be an isolated incident. It feels like the pressure is constant now.

You've had this low mood for three months without any improvement, but considering the significant stress you're under with your husband's health, do you think if the stressors were to decrease or be managed better, you might see an improvement in your mood, or does the feeling of emptiness and lack of interest seem independent of these external factors?

Caring for my husband is incredibly stressful, but this low mood feels like a heavy, empty crash that has taken on a life of its own. Even when I have quiet moments, that emptiness and complete lack of interest in my painting or gardening remain constant, like a deep fog that won't lift just by managing the stress.

Given your current experience and the fact that this is your first episode of low mood, do you think the duration and severity of your symptoms might be related to the duration of your husband's illness and the caregiving responsibilities, or could there be other underlying factors contributing to your persistent low mood?

The caregiving responsibilities and my husband's declining health have been incredibly heavy burdens over the past year, especially when I was losing sleep managing his medications and appointments before my high spell. This heavy, low feeling has been going on for about three months now since I crashed, and while the stress of caregiving was definitely the trigger, I feel so completely stuck and exhausted that it feels like something deeper has taken over.
Have you experienced any thoughts of hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, or having beliefs that seem unrealistic to others during this period of low mood?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I haven't heard any strange voices, seen things that aren't there, or held any unusual or unrealistic beliefs during this low period. Aside from my mind feeling blank and tired, I haven't had those kinds of experiences.

You've mentioned this is your first experience with a prolonged low mood, but considering the duration of three months without any improvement, do you think this episode might be more related to a persistent depressive disorder or a single major depressive episode?

I'm sorry, but I don't really understand those medical terms like "persistent depressive disorder" or "major depressive episode" since I don't have any medical background. All I know is that I had that highly energetic, busy period in the spring before crashing into this heavy, low feeling three months ago. I'll have to leave figuring out those kinds of diagnoses up to you.

Given that you've had no previous episodes like this and the current episode has lasted for three months without any improvement, do you think if the current stressors in your life were to significantly decrease, you might expect your mood to improve, or do you fear that this low mood could become a recurring issue for you?

I’m really not sure, to be honest. Right now, this heavy feeling is so overwhelming that it's hard to imagine it lifting even if things got easier with my husband's care. I just don't know what the future holds or if this is something I'll have to keep dealing with.

Do you think that if your husband's health were to stabilize or improve, and the caregiving burden were to lessen, you would likely return to your normal self and activities, or do you fear that this low mood might persist even with reduced stress?
I'm really not sure about that. Right now, I just feel too exhausted and overwhelmed to even think about the future or how I might feel if the caregiving load changed.

Considering your current low mood has lasted three months without improvement, and given the significant stress you're under, do you think this episode might be part of a larger pattern of mood swings, or does it feel like an isolated incident triggered by the caregiving stress?

Looking back, it does feel like part of a larger pattern of mood swings rather than just an isolated incident. This current three-month low directly followed that highly unusual, "revved up" spell in the spring where I had endless energy and overcommitted at the community center. The extreme contrast between that high period and this current crash makes it feel like my mood is swinging between two opposite extremes.

Given that you've experienced a significant shift from a high-energy state to a low mood, and considering this is your first such experience, do you think the fact that this low mood has lasted for three months without any periods of improvement suggests it might be a single episode, or could this be indicative of a pattern that might recur in the future?

I'm really not sure whether this will be a recurring pattern or just a one-time thing, since I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. Right now, I'm just completely overwhelmed by how long this low period has lasted, which has been about three months now. I really don't know what to expect for the future.

You mentioned that this is your first experience with such a significant mood shift, but considering the duration and the fact that it followed a period of high energy, do you think that if you were to experience another period of high energy in the future, it might be followed by another episode of low mood, or do you believe this is an isolated incident?

I honestly don't know what the future holds or if this will happen again. My mind feels so tired and sluggish right now that I haven't really thought about it. I'm just trying to get through each day, so I really can't say.

Can you clarify if you believe the current low mood episode is directly linked to the stress of caregiving for your husband, or do you think it might be a more intrinsic issue that could recur even if the caregiving stress were to decrease?

I'm really not sure about that. While caring for my husband has been incredibly stressful and exhausting, I don't know if this severe low mood is entirely because of that stress or if it's something deeper. I've never experienced these extreme highs and lows like this before, so I really can't tell.

Do you think that even if your husband's health improves and the caregiving burden lessens, you might still experience episodes of low mood or is this low mood inextricably linked to the current stressors in your life?

I'm really not sure about that. I feel so overwhelmed right now by everything that it's hard to imagine how I would feel even if the stress lessened. Because of that, I haven't really thought about whether this low mood is entirely tied to the caregiving or not.

Do you think that if you were to experience a full recovery from this current episode of low mood, you would be at risk of having another episode in the future, or do you believe that addressing the current stressors and this episode would prevent future occurrences?

I'm really not sure how these mood cycles work or if addressing the stress would prevent another episode in the future. This is all so new to me, and I honestly don't know what to expect. Right now, I'm just trying to focus on getting through this heavy, low feeling day by day.

Do you think that the fact this is your first episode of low mood, which has lasted three months without improvement, might suggest it's a single major depressive episode, or could the pattern of shifting from high energy to low mood indicate a potential for future episodes?

There was definitely a very clear shift from being extremely wound up and high-energy in the spring to crashing into this heavy, low mood for the past three months. While I'm not sure what this means for the future, this pattern of going from one extreme to the other is exactly what my family and I have observed, and it feels like more than just a simple bout of depression.

Do you think the fact that you've had no previous episodes like this, but now you've experienced a significant high followed by a three-month low, suggests that if you were to recover from this episode, you might still be at risk for future episodes of either high or low mood?

I'm really not sure and I haven't really thought about the possibility of having more of these episodes in the future. I am just feeling too exhausted and overwhelmed by how I feel right now to think about what might happen down the road.

Have you ever had any periods of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, even if brief, where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or had decreased need for sleep, aside from the highly energetic period you mentioned in the spring?

No, I don't recall ever having another period of feeling unusually energetic, elevated, or irritable prior to the episode in the spring. As far as I can remember, that spring spell was the only time in my life I have ever felt that way.
Can you describe in more detail what you mean by 'mood swings' and if you've noticed any patterns or triggers for these shifts in your mood?

Starting in the spring, the stress of caring for my husband and sleeping less triggered a highly 'revved up' period where I was overly active, talkative, and irritable. That high spell then abruptly ended, and I crashed into this heavy, low period where I've lost interest in everything. This low phase has now lasted for about three months.
Can you tell me more about the 'highly revved up' period in the spring, such as how long it lasted and if you experienced any impulsivity or reckless behavior during that time?

That "revved up" period lasted for about a month in the spring before I suddenly crashed into this low mood. I didn't do anything wild or dangerous, but I was extremely impulsive about overcommitting myself—trying to start multiple new art projects at the community center, rearranging our house, and neglecting my own doctor appointments because I felt like I didn't need any rest.

Do you think the pattern of shifting from a high-energy state to a low mood, as you've experienced this year, might indicate a potential for future episodes of either high or low mood, or does this feel like an isolated incident to you?

I'm really not sure and I haven't thought much about whether this could happen again in the future. Right now, I am just feeling so overwhelmed by this present low mood that I'm focusing entirely on trying to get through each day. It is hard to imagine what might happen down the road when I feel so heavy and tired today.

Can you recall any other times in your life, aside from the spring episode, where you felt extremely energetic, talkative, or had decreased need for sleep for several days, even if it wasn't as severe as the spring episode?
No, I don't recall ever having another period like that in my life before this past spring. Other than that one time, I've otherwise generally felt like my normal self over the years.

Do you think the extreme contrast between your high-energy period in the spring and this current low mood could be indicative of a bipolar disorder, given the significant shift in your mood and energy levels?

The contrast between those two periods has been incredibly stark. In the spring, I felt unusually driven and energized, almost like a completely different person, but now I feel totally drained and unable to care about anything. While I didn't think of "bipolar disorder" myself, looking back at how extreme that shift was makes me realize that explanation actually makes a lot of sense.
